meta.title: Prompt Critical: a Minecraft mod with real reactor physics
meta.description: Prompt Critical is a NeoForge 1.21.1 mod about heavy industry, from the coal mine to the nuclear fuel cycle. Try its reactor kinetics in the browser and see real runs of the physics core.

meta.title: Prompt Critical guide: from the first coal to the reactor
meta.description: How progress works in Prompt Critical: finding coal, first steam, the mine, the hoist, the longwall and the foundry, then steel, oil, chemistry and the atom. Step by step, with numbers and screenshots.

guide.foot: Screenshots: development build with Complementary Reimagined shaders. Numbers come from the in-game engineering handbook; for I1–I4 they are plans and will change.

lead.h1: A reactor is not a block that outputs RF.
lead.lede: Prompt Critical is a Minecraft mod about heavy industry, from the coal mine to the closed nuclear fuel cycle. Its physics core runs real equations. The desk on this page runs the same reactor kinetics in your browser.
lead.task: The reactor is shut down, rods fully inserted. Bring it to 100 % power and hold it within ±5 % for 15 seconds.
lead.hint1: Pull the rods slowly. Power rises exponentially, and the period meter tells you how fast.
lead.hint2: Protection trips the reactor if the period drops below 5 s or power passes 118 %. It does not ask.
lead.hint3: Curious what prompt critical looks like? Bypass protection. Then don't.

sim.label: Reactor control desk
sim.canvasLabel: Reactor power on a log scale and rod position over the last two minutes of simulated time
sim.fine_html: Six delayed-neutron groups for U-235 (Keepin), β = 0.0065, Λ = 20 µs: the constants from pc-sim's DelayedNeutronData, integrated implicitly in 1 ms steps. Temperature feedback here is a one-line toy; in the mod it comes from the thermal-hydraulic model.
sim.st_ready: Shut down. Rods in. Start withdrawing.
sim.st_sub: Subcritical: power settles at a higher level but won't grow on its own. Keep withdrawing, slowly.
sim.st_critical: Critical. Power is rising on its own; watch the period.
sim.st_done: Shift complete: 100 % held for 15 s, reached in {t} of simulated time.
sim.st_trip: Reactor trip: {why}. Rods dropped by gravity. Press Reset to start over.
sim.st_damage: Fuel damage. With protection bypassed, power ran away faster than the fuel could shed heat. This is why the trip does not ask.

prompt.h: Why the mod is named after the scariest term in reactor physics
prompt.p1: Only 0.65 % of neutrons from U-235 fission arrive late, seconds to a minute after the fission. Those few delayed neutrons are what makes a reactor controllable: they stretch the time between generations from microseconds to something a human, or a relay cabinet, can react to.
prompt.p2: Once the reactivity reaches one dollar (β), the chain reaction no longer waits for them. That point is prompt criticality. Below it you steer the reactor. Above it, nothing steers it.
prompt.pullNote: reactor period after a +0.1 $ step, with and without delayed neutrons
prompt.figCap: Inhour equation for U-235, Λ = 20 µs, computed by pc-sim. Log scale.

tests.h: Test runs. Nobody scripted these curves.
tests.sub: Every chart below is a run of pc-sim, the pure-Java physics core of the mod: no Minecraft, no hand-drawn curves. The data regenerates with ./gradlew :pc-sim:siteData.
tests.lofTitle: PR-300 test plant loses a pump.
tests.lofCap: 300 MW, two loops. Pump B loses power at 5 s; coastdown, flow redistribution and the trip come out of the equations.
tests.ev1: Pump B loses power and starts to coast down.
tests.ev2: Protection trips on low coolant flow, 2 out of 3 channels.
tests.ev3: Power is down to 6 %. Minimum DNBR in the transient: 4.16, the trip setpoint is 1.45.
tests.ev4: The idle loop flows backwards: loop A pushes water through it at −16 %.
tests.scramTitle: SCRAM: the reactor keeps making heat.
tests.scramCap: Fission power from a pc-sim run with a manual trip at 5 s. Decay heat is a Way–Wigner estimate, not yet modeled in pc-sim. Log scale.
tests.waterTitle: Why water boils at 345 °C in a PWR.
tests.waterCap: Saturation line from pc-sim's IAPWS-IF97 tables. At 15.5 MPa, the pressure of a typical PWR primary loop, water boils at about 345 °C.
tests.perfLabel: mean per tick for the whole coupled PR-300 plant
tests.perfAria: Measured tick time compared with the 3 ms per tick budget
tests.perfNote: {n} ticks after warm-up: p50 {p50} ms, p95 {p95} ms, p99 {p99} ms. Measured on a developer machine, so treat it as an order of magnitude.

industry.h: Five industries. Each one feeds the next.
industry.sub: You don't unlock a reactor with a recipe. You build the industry that can make its parts.
industry.i0p: A coal mine with methane and ventilation, coal boilers, a steam engine driving a Create shaft.
industry.i1p: Coke ovens, blast furnace, converter, seamless pipes. Synchronous generators, power lines, transformers, protection relays. The first graphite pile.
industry.i2p: Seismic survey, drilling and well control, a refinery, gas processing, gas turbines.
industry.i3p: Pyrolysis, polymers, chlor-alkali, syngas, ion-exchange resins, TBP for fuel reprocessing.
industry.i4p: An enrichment cascade, fuel assemblies, reprocessing, isotopes and RTGs.
industry.ladderSub: The mod gives you sensors, function blocks and peripherals. The control system is yours to design, and it grows with the plant.
industry.a0: Manual: valves, switches and a person watching gauges.
industry.a1: Relay logic: interlocks wired in a cabinet.
industry.a3: PLCs in IEC 61131-3 languages and safety instrumented systems.
industry.a4: DCS and SCADA on CC: Tweaked computers.
industry.artNote: Block renders are placeholder art from the Blockbench sources in the repository.

status.has1: pc-sim: reactor kinetics, IAPWS-IF97 water and steam, the two-loop PR-300 test plant, hardware protection.
status.has2: Era I0 in the game: a fire-tube boiler and a steam engine on a Create shaft; a mine with ventilation, methane and explosions; hoisting, drainage, a longwall, coal washing, a foundry and machine tools; the engineering handbook.
status.has3: The NeoForge mod skeleton, CI, architecture tests that keep pc-sim free of Minecraft code.
status.has4: Placeholder models for the blocks across all five industries.
status.has5: The design document; the wiki summarizes it.
status.not1: Eras I1–I4. Steel, oil, chemistry and a reactor in the world are still design only.
status.not2: Releases. There is nothing to download.
status.follow: Follow the build. Devlogs and short reactor-physics videos are on YouTube.
